brief: GS Prime's weekly rundown: the S&P fell 2.7% as investors reacted to post-midterm opposition to data center development, which raised worries about a widening supply-demand gap in the data center supply chain. Semis (SOX down 28% over 22 days) and Memory/Optical Networks led losses, while Goldminers, ACA names and Homebuilders outperformed. Wednesday's post-midterm relief rally left clients underhedged, so Thursday's reversal pushed the desk's vol panic index to 9.57 out of 10, the 3rd largest daily jump ever, following the 4th largest drop on Wednesday. ETF notional volume hit $580bn, the third largest day on record, and put volume hit a record 11mm-plus contracts, while the VIX curve flipped into backwardation. Hedge funds cut gross leverage 8.7 points, the largest drop since Covid, to 207.5%, and net leverage fell to a 5-year-low 43.3%, led by heavy Info Tech and Industrials selling. CTA trend signals turned negative in 60% of global equity markets, and GS expects CTAs to sell $28bn of SPX futures next week. Flows rotated into defensives (XLU, XLV, XLP), even as GS recommends shorting its own Staples basket on stretched valuations. Investors are increasingly pricing AI capex buildouts further out, toward 2028 and beyond.
